answer: Temporal diversity at the onyx: each identity draws a randomized submission window, so a sybil farm must hold keys live across all epochs. The lotus score enforces this — credit accrues only to windows that are unpredictably timed. An attacker sustaining k identities pays roughly k × 500 CPU-hours plus coordination latency, and the canyon of missed windows collapses their yield below honest single-node returns before k=20. Works because unpredictable timing makes bulk key-holding strictly costlier than genuine diversity.
